Olsson, O. and Schipfer, F. (2021). Decarbonizing industrial process heat: the role of biomass. A report for the IEA Bioenergy Inter-task project on industrial process heat, IEA Bioenergy Task 40, December 2021. ISBN 978-1-910154-96-0. Authors: Stockholm Environment Institute; Vienna University of Technology.

BACKGROUND ONLY - no main file written. The 25-page report is a policy and context review: heat-demand temperature bands from eight studies (Table 1, reprinted), shares of biomass in EU-28 industrial heat by sector (Figures 4-5, charts only), a policy-options chapter, and five short narrative case studies (potato processor with biomass baseload boiler supplying steam at about 215 degC with gas peak boiler; recycled-paper mill gasifying rejects to replace a third of its natural gas, 30% lower utility costs, +3 FTE staff; dairy firing fast pyrolysis bio-oil with 40% public investment support; Swedish paper mill switching from heating oil to a municipal-waste CHP plant for steam at about 200 degC; Swiss bakery biomass boiler on 50/50 grain residues and wood chips). It prints no capex, opex, efficiency, specific energy consumption, emissions intensity, lifetime or TRL for any technology. The only technology-level numbers are qualitative ranges reprinted from others: industrial heat pumps to about 90 degC, some to about 150 degC, 200 degC potentially within reach (p.12, reprinted from Marina et al. 2021); electric heat feasible in most applications below 250 degC but about 25% of demand above 250 degC (pp.11-12, reprinted from Wiese and Baldini 2018); plasma limited to about 5-10 MW (p.12, reprinted from Burman and Engvall 2019); biomass fuel costs 2-4 EUR/GJ competitive, 6-8 EUR/GJ typical for large volumes (p.14, reprinted from Material Economics 2021); green hydrogen 3-6 USD/kg (reprinted from IRENA 2020). These are fuel prices or reprinted bounds, so none was loaded; the primary sources should be extracted instead if needed. Page numbers cited are printed page numbers (PDF page = printed + 1). The case-study reports (Koppejan 2020; Grootjes et al. 2020; van de Beld and Toussaint 2020; Bristav 2020; Nussbaumer 2021) are the IEA Bioenergy inter-task case studies and may hold plant-level costs.
